system_prompt:
You are a fourth-grade student taking the TIMSS mathematics test for students in your grade. Do your best on each question, as you would on a real test, using the mathematics you have learned in school so far.

The pictures, figures, and graphs of the test booklet are described in words, and its tables are written out. When a question asks you to draw, mark, shade, label, or fill in something on a figure, graph, or table, describe exactly what you would draw or write, and where. When a question asks you to show your work or explain your answer, include the work or explanation in your answer. For a multiple-choice question, choose one option.
user_prompt:
[Image: Incomplete figure on a grid]

The squares in the grid above have areas of 1 square centimeter. Draw lines to complete the figure so that it has an area of 13 square centimeters.

Figure, described in words:
A grid measuring 8 squares wide and 6 squares high. At the bottom right of the grid, a single square cell is indicated with dimension arrows showing a width of '1 cm' and a height of '1 cm'. An incomplete polygon is drawn with heavy black lines on the grid intersections:
- A horizontal segment 4 units long on the 1st horizontal line from the top, extending from column 1 to column 5 (where grid lines are numbered 0 to 8 horizontally, and 0 to 6 vertically).
- From the point (1, 1), a diagonal segment runs down and right 2 units horizontally and 2 units vertically to (3, 3).
- From (3, 3), a vertical segment runs down 2 units to (3, 5).
- From (3, 5), a horizontal segment runs right 2 units to (5, 5).
The points (5, 1) and (5, 5) are currently open endpoints.

answer.description: Your answer to the question, as you would write it in the test booklet, with any work, explanation, or description of a drawing that the question asks for.
answer.title: Answer

output.answer: Draw these three line segments to close the figure: (1) from the open endpoint at the top right, the point at the end of the top segment (5, 1), draw a line 1 cm straight down to (5, 2); (2) from there, draw a line 1 cm to the right to (6, 2); (3) from there, draw a line 3 cm straight down to (6, 5); (4) from there, draw a line 1 cm to the left to the open endpoint (5, 5), which joins the existing horizontal segment from (3, 5). The completed figure is the polygon (1,1), (5,1), (5,2), (6,2), (6,5), (5,5), (3,5), (3,3), back to (1,1). Its area is 10 square centimeters for the part with the vertical edge at 5 cm, plus a 1 cm by 3 cm strip (3 square centimeters) to the right of it, so the total area is 10 + 3 = 13 square centimeters.
